pr.title: Dismiss a settled change request once every model finds the head clean
pr.head: fbe116df79105a7625f09dc31be0589e9f9e58c6

summary: Projector's review loop posts each review as one GitHub account, and several models can review the same pull request under that account. On another author's pull request, a changes-requested verdict posts a real REQUEST_CHANGES review, which sets GitHub's reviewDecision, the status that blocks a merge. A later clean verdict posts only a COMMENT unless review.allow_approve is on, and a COMMENT replaces nothing. So the pull request stayed at CHANGES_REQUESTED after every model had found the head clean, and fix-pr kept reporting a change request that no finding backed.

This change makes project review publish dismiss those change requests. After it posts a review on another author's pull request, it lists the account's Projector REQUEST_CHANGES reviews that are still standing. When the sign-off rule says the head is clean, it dismisses each one as the reviewer, then reads them back to confirm. The sign-off rule is the existing check that every model's newest verdict on the head is clean, no model is still reviewing it, and no finding thread is open.

The first review found that the code recognized a Projector change request by the text projector-review anywhere in its body, so a hand-written change request that mentioned the loop by name was dismissed too. The author fixed it: a change request now counts only when its body carries a verdict marker line, the same test the sign-off rule uses. The review of this head is clean.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Standing change request: a REQUEST_CHANGES review by the reviewer's account that nobody dismissed and no later APPROVE by the account replaced.
  • Sign-off: the result of the sign-off rule for a head, one of clean, waiting, changes-requested, or unreviewed.
  • Peer wait: up to review.peer_wait seconds (180 by default) that publish waits for another model that reviewed an earlier head and has not started on this one.

cards.title: What publish does on another author's pull request
cards.html:
SituationResult
Every model clean on the headDismisses the standing Projector change requests
Another model requests changes or is reviewingDismisses nothing
A peer that reviewed an earlier head posts nothing within the waitDismisses, including that peer's change request
An APPROVE came after the change requestDismisses nothing
A change request without a Projector markerStays
GitHub refuses the dismissalExits 1 with the lock held; a rerun finishes

groups.title: Dismissal in publish
groups.kicker: How publish finds and dismisses the account's standing change requests
intro: standing_change_requests reads every review on the pull request by the reviewer's account, in order. An APPROVE clears the list, because an approval already replaces the earlier change requests in reviewDecision. Each Projector REQUEST_CHANGES after it joins the list. A dismissed review has the state DISMISSED, so it never appears.

publish calls it after the review is posted, and only on another author's pull request, since GitHub refuses REQUEST_CHANGES on your own. A standing change request now makes publish wait for peers, as a draft does on a self-review. When the sign-off is clean and the head did not move during the wait, dismiss sends each dismissal with the reviewer's token, and then lists the change requests again to confirm that none still stands. A failure raises before the start comment is deleted, so a rerun of publish finishes the job without posting a second review.

checks.text: The full suite passes at this head: 761 tests, 1 skipped, with project check, both claude plugin validate runs, and git diff --check clean.

files.note: Adds standing_change_requests and dismiss, and calls them from publish after the sign-off rule runs.

checks.text: A change request counts as Projector's only when verdict_marker finds a marker line in its body. I reran a reproduction at this head with the fake GitHub: a hand-written change request reading "The projector-review loop missed the empty case" stays CHANGES_REQUESTED after a clean publish.

The peer wait now applies on another author's pull request whenever a standing change request exists. When this review's own verdict is changes-requested, the sign-off is not clean, so sign returns at once and nothing waits.

The list of change requests to dismiss is taken before the peer wait. A change request that a peer posts during the wait is not in the list, and it also turns the sign-off to changes-requested, so nothing is dismissed.

files.note: Prints a dismissed change request … line when publish dismissed any.

groups.title: Dismissal tests
groups.kicker: Six cases against the fake GitHub
intro: The fake GitHub in tests/test_review.py now returns each review's state, so the code can tell an approval from a change request, and answers the dismissal call by marking the review DISMISSED. DismissalTests sets up another author's pull request where claude-opus-5-5 requested changes on an earlier head.

checks.text: This test pins the case where a peer that requested changes on an earlier head posts nothing within 180 seconds: publish treats it as absent and dismisses its change request too. That matches how a self-review marks a draft ready after the same wait.
